definition: Furtive means done secretly or stealthily, in a way that suggests hidden or guilty intent.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word furtive. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know furtive should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: He slid the report into his bag with a furtive glance toward the supervisor's office.
Discreet is weaker than furtive: a discreet person keeps things quiet out of tact, with nothing to hide, while a furtive one moves as if caught halfway through a guilty act.
Clandestine is stronger than furtive — clandestine describes whole operations kept deliberately hidden, while furtive describes the darting, guilty manner of a single glance or gesture.

Stealthy means quiet and careful to escape notice — a technique of silent movement, whatever the purpose. Furtive adds the look of guilt: a furtive glance is not just quiet but shifty, as if its owner fears being caught at something. Stealth is a method; a furtive manner is a tell.

Sneaky means acting slyly and deceptively in secret, usually to get away with something — it judges the behavior. Furtive describes how that secrecy looks from the outside: the darting glance or half-hidden movement that suggests guilty intent. A sneaky plan is the scheme; the furtive manner is what betrays it.
